summary: 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry and active AAPS settings demonstrates exceptionally strong glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.3% Time Above Range, and 0.0% Time Below Range. Basal delivery, target segments, ISF, DIA (5.5h), and loop safety limits are well matched to underlying physiology. The primary opportunity for refinement is optimization of meal prebolus timing and immediate bolus split for weekend brunch to attenuate transient postprandial peaks (up to 188 mg/dL) that currently resolve cleanly to baseline within 240 minutes.

analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid CGM entries over 14 days with 100.0% coverage and zero data gaps exceeding 15 minutes.
analysis_steps.findings: Data completeness and cadence are optimal for comprehensive profile and automation analysis.

analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%, Time in Range 99.7%, Time Above Range 0.3%, Time Below Range 0.0%.
analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding overall safety with zero clinical hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) recorded. Glycemic variability is low.

analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local mean glucose between 102.3 and 107.5 mg/dL across 00:00-05:00 local time.
analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal rates hold glucose stable during overnight fasting without triggering excessive low-temp corrections or nocturnal lows.

analysis_steps.evidence: 28 meal boluses analyzed. Weekday breakfast returns to baseline (-14 to +8 mg/dL) at 240m; weekend brunch returns to baseline (-11 to +1 mg/dL) at 240m.
analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios, ISF, and 5.5h DIA are accurate. Weekend brunch experiences a temporary 120-minute peak (up to 188 mg/dL) due to timing/split rather than a CR deficit.

analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM enabled; 3-minute interval, 45-minute max SMB basal minutes, 30-minute max UAM SMB basal minutes.
analysis_steps.findings: SMB/UAM automation provides safe postprandial micro-dosing without causing insulin stacking or secondary hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Raw boolean toggles for specific SMB triggers are null in profile export, but core SMB delivery is active and verified.

analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U, min_5m_carbimpact 3 mg/dL/5 min, meal_max_absorption_hours 6.0 h.
analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits and carb absorption settings are appropriate and aligned with insulin DIA.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens explicit boolean flags are null in export; Dynamic ISF adjustment factor is set at 100%.

analysis_steps.evidence: Declared strategy: Weekday breakfast uses 20m prebolus / 70% immediate split; Weekend brunch uses 10m prebolus / 60% immediate split with 20g e-carbs over 120m.
analysis_steps.findings: Weekday breakfast strategy keeps postprandial glucose under 167 mg/dL. Weekend brunch allows higher peak excursions (188 mg/dL) due to shorter prebolus and lower immediate split.

analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show complete glucose normalization at 240m for extended carb entries.
analysis_steps.findings: E-carb duration and absorption parameters align well with physiological meal decay and DIA.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of telemetry data, active profile, and user-declared strategies across all workflow steps.
analysis_steps.findings: All core profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) are performant and should remain unchanged. Behavioral adjustment of prebolus timing for weekend brunch is recommended prior to any parameter changes.

strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL).
Extremely low overall glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%.
Highly stable overnight glucose maintenance averaging 102-107 mg/dL.
Well-calibrated Carb Ratios and DIA resulting in complete 4-hour postprandial recovery.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peaks up to 188 mg/dL following weekend brunch (10:30 UTC window).

recommendations.title: Extend Prebolus Timing for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch currently exhibits 120-minute postprandial peaks up to 188 mg/dL before returning cleanly to baseline at 240 minutes. Extending the prebolus window from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes and increasing the immediate bolus split from 60% to 70% will suppress the initial glucose spike without risking late hypoglycemia.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA profile settings as currently configured.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Glycemic outcomes are near-optimal with 99.7% TIR and 0% hypoglycemia. 4-hour postprandial glucose returns cleanly to baseline across all meal windows, demonstrating total dosage accuracy across all Carb Ratios.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Evaluate 2-hour postprandial peak after extending weekend brunch prebolus to 15-20 minutes.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Utilize a 15-20 minute prebolus combined with a 70% immediate bolus split and 30% e-carbs (or SMB/UAM automation) for optimal postprandial control.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Data across 28 treatments shows that 4-hour postprandial recovery is excellent, but 2-hour peaks are sensitive to prebolus timing and initial split.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor peak glucose at 120 minutes following weekend brunch after applying a 15-20 minute prebolus.

exceptions.suggestion: Increase prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes and immediate bolus split from 60% to 70%.
exceptions.rationale: Current 10-minute prebolus allows transient spikes up to 188 mg/dL that resolve cleanly by 240m, confirming total insulin requirement is accurate.

implementation_steps: Retain all existing basal rates, CRs, ISFs, target segments, and DIA settings in the active profile.
For weekend brunch meals, administer the bolus 15 to 20 minutes prior to eating instead of 10 minutes.
Adjust the immediate bolus percentage for weekend brunch from 60% to 70%.
Observe postprandial glucose peaks over the subsequent 2 to 3 weekend brunch cycles to verify peak reduction below 160 mg/dL without post-meal hypoglycemia.
education: When 4-hour postprandial glucose returns cleanly to starting levels, the total insulin amount (Carb Ratio) is correct; early 2-hour spikes are driven by bolus timing relative to carb absorption.
